Section 1

What changes in sales and marketing at Level 5

Who it is for. People who lead a sales, marketing or account management team, such as a sales manager, marketing manager or account management lead.

In a sales or marketing team, AI now drafts outreach emails, proposals, campaign copy and social posts. Automated lead scoring ranks the inbound list. CRM records fill themselves from calls and emails. A weekly report that took a day now takes minutes. The work left is checking what comes back and deciding what goes out under the team's name. It is also judging which leads and accounts deserve a person's time.

That changes the content of each role. A business development representative may write fewer first emails and qualify more replies. A content producer may edit more than they draft. An account manager may start a renewal with a briefing already built. Some established skills matter less. New ones matter more, such as checking a generated claim before it is published.

The person leading the function decides how far to take this. Their evidence is the team's own pipeline, campaign and account figures. They answer for what the team sends, says and records. Rules on electronic marketing, personal data and advertising claims all apply. Choosing which markets to sell into is not theirs to decide here. Where the change needs that, it is recorded as a constraint or a dependency.

The same qualification. A learner on this version is assessed against the same criteria, to the same assessment model, as a learner on the generic Diploma. Only the context differs. Their own department is the evidence.

Section 3

The rules sales and marketing works within

A department changing its work stays inside these. The learner records each one where the units ask for constraints and obligations, and works within it.

UK GDPR. CRM records of prospects and customers are personal data. Scoring them automatically or passing them to an AI tool needs a lawful basis. It is a constraint at ZFF-AU-05 1.4 and an obligation at ZFF-PJ-05 1.6.

Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations 2003 (PECR). Marketing emails and texts to individual subscribers need consent unless the soft opt-in applies: an existing customer, similar products, and an opt-out offered when details were collected and in every message. Emails to corporate addresses do not need consent but must identify the sender and give an address for opting out. Who may be contacted belongs in the checks at ZFF-AU-05 5.1 and the obligations at ZFF-PJ-05 1.6.

CAP Code (UK Code of Non-broadcast Advertising and Direct & Promotional Marketing). Marketing must not mislead, and marketers must hold evidence for objective claims before publication. AI-drafted copy can state things nobody can evidence, so a human check on claims is recorded at ZFF-AU-05 5.1 and ZFF-PJ-05 4.4.

Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. It prohibits unfair commercial practices towards consumers, including fake reviews. Where the team sells to consumers, generated reviews or testimonials are risks to record at ZFF-AU-05 5.2 and ZFF-PJ-05 4.6.

Equality Act 2010. When roles change, a disabled colleague may need reasonable adjustments to the new work. That shapes the support at ZFF-EI-05 4.4 and ZFF-GM-05 4.5, within the obligations identified at ZFF-EI-05 1.5.

Trade Union and Labour Relations (Consolidation) Act 1992. Proposing to dismiss 20 or more employees as redundant at one establishment within 90 days requires collective consultation with appropriate representatives (section 188). That includes dismissing and re-engaging people to change their terms. The Employment Rights Act 2025 is changing these duties, so check what is in force. Recorded at ZFF-EI-05 1.5.

ZFF-GM-05

Leading a Department Through a Change in Required Capability

Level5TQT60 hoursCredits6GLH24 indicativeStatusMandatoryCriteria28

In Sales and marketing

Here the change is in what sales and marketing people are expected to be good at. Writing a first draft matters less when AI produces one. Checking it, editing it to the team's standard and judging whether to send it matter more. The learner establishes what the team can do today from its own records. They determine what it will need, then lead the people through the change.

Learning outcomes and assessment criteria

LO1
The learner will: Know how a change in required capability affects the work of a department.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
1.1Analyse the effects on a department's work when the capabilities its roles require change, including the effect on people whose established competence is no longer what the work requires
1.2Compare different approaches to building capability in a department, and the reasoning behind each
1.3Evaluate the reasons capability-building programmes fail to change what people do at work
1.4Identify the constraints that limit what own department can change about the capability it holds, including time, budget, role definitions, agreements and the availability of learning
1.5Evaluate the different views held within own department about the change in what its people are expected to be good at, and the reasoning given for them

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner analyses what happens when skills like writing outreach from scratch stop being what the work needs (1.1). They compare ways to build capability, such as call coaching or peer review of drafts (1.2). They evaluate why sales training so often fails to change calls (1.3). Commission plans, role definitions, budget and the campaign calendar are constraints at 1.4, and the team's views are weighed at 1.5.

LO2
The learner will: Be able to establish what capability a department holds and what it will require.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
2.1Determine the method used to establish what capability the department holds and what it will require, and state the reasons for choosing it
2.2Establish the capabilities the department's roles currently require, and the work each of those capabilities supports
2.3Establish the capability the department currently holds, using the department's own records and evidence from work already carried out
2.4Determine the capability the department will require as its processes change, and state the reasons
2.5Analyse the difference between the capability held and the capability required, and identify where that difference carries most cost to the department
2.6Evaluate the reliability of the evidence obtained, and state how gaps were handled

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner determines how to establish capability, such as reviewing real proposals and call notes rather than a self-rating survey (2.1). They establish what each role requires (2.2) and what the team can already do from its records (2.3). They determine what drafting, scoring and reporting will require next (2.4). They find where the gap costs most, such as rework on proposals (2.5), and how far the evidence holds (2.6).

LO3
The learner will: Be able to determine how a department's capability difference will be closed.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
3.1Determine the criteria against which options for closing the difference will be evaluated, and state the reasons for them
3.2Identify the options available for closing each part of the difference, including developing the people already in post, changing how work is allocated, recruiting, redeploying, and obtaining capability from outside the department
3.3Interpret the cost and the benefit of each option, using figures from the department's own systems
3.4Use relevant investigation of comparable work, inside or outside own organisation, to inform the choice between options
3.5Identify a capability the department should not attempt to build, and evaluate the reasons
3.6Evaluate the options against the criteria determined at 3.1, and state which are recommended

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner sets the criteria for judging options before looking at any (3.1). Options include coaching, moving research work between roles, recruiting or using an agency (3.2). Costs and benefits come from the team's own figures (3.3) and from comparable teams (3.4). They name a capability not to build, such as in-house video, with reasons (3.5). Then they recommend against their own criteria (3.6).

LO4
The learner will: Be able to lead a department through a change in what its people are expected to be good at.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
4.1Identify the people whose expected capability changes, and state how it changes for each
4.2Consult those people about the change, and record what was raised
4.3Analyse the concerns raised, and evaluate which of them alter the recommended options
4.4Adapt the recommendation in response to what the consultation established, and state what changed
4.5State, for each person whose expected capability changes, the actions they are expected to take, the support available to them and the period over which the change applies
4.6Determine how the change in the department's capability will be evidenced in the work the department produces, and state what will count as evidence

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner identifies who is affected, such as representatives known for writing outreach by hand (4.1), and consults them (4.2). A common concern is that commission will dip while new skills bed in. The learner decides whether such concerns change the recommendation (4.3) and adapts it (4.4). Each person gets actions, support and a period (4.5), and the learner decides what output will show the change (4.6).

LO5
The learner will: Be able to evaluate a change in a department's capability and own method.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
5.1Evaluate the change in the department's capability against the requirement determined at 2.4, using the evidence determined at 4.6
5.2Evaluate the effect of the change on the work the department produces, using figures from the department's own systems
5.3Identify where the change did not take effect, and evaluate the reasons
5.4Evaluate how effective the method determined at 2.1 and the criteria determined at 3.1 were, giving reasons
5.5Identify what would be determined differently at the next change in the department's required capability, and the reasons

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner evaluates the change against the requirement at 2.4, using the evidence chosen at 4.6 (5.1). They evaluate the effect on the team's work from its own CRM or campaign reports (5.2). They find where it did not take, such as one territory still writing by hand (5.3). They review their method and criteria (5.4) and what they would decide differently next time (5.5).

5 learning outcomes, 28 assessment criteria. The same criteria as the generic Diploma, word for word.

Evidence from Sales and marketing work

  • 2.1, 2.3, 2.6. A capability record built from a sample of the team's own proposals and call notes. It gives the reasons for that method and notes gaps, such as roles with no recent work.
  • 2.4, 2.5. A statement of what the team will need once AI drafts first outreach. The gap is costed in the team's own terms, such as hours of rework on proposals.
  • 3.1, 3.3, 3.6. The learner's own criteria for choosing between coaching, reallocation, recruitment and agency support. It includes costs from the team's systems and a recommendation.
  • 4.2, 4.3, 4.4. A consultation record with colleagues identified by role, and the concerns raised about targets and commission. The revised recommendation shows what changed.
  • 4.5. A short note for each affected role. It sets out the expected actions, the support available and the period it covers.
  • 5.1, 5.2, 5.3. A review using at least one measurement taken after the change, against the evidence set at 4.6. It states its period and limits, and names where the change did not take effect.

Keeping it at Level 5

It drops to Level 4 when a supplied sales competency framework or a fixed training list decides 2.1 and 3.1. It rises above Level 5 when the learner redesigns how the organisation sells, instead of recording that need at 1.4.

The unit aim, level check, boundaries, assessment guidance and evidence trail are in ZFF-GM-05 on the generic Diploma, and apply here unchanged.

ZFF-EI-05

Working with the People Whose Roles Change

Level5TQT60 hoursCredits6GLH24 indicativeStatusMandatoryCriteria27

In Sales and marketing

Sales and marketing roles change when AI drafts the emails and automated scoring routes the leads. Some people welcome it. Others see the part of the job they were best at, and paid for, being taken over. The learner works with all of them, including those who do not accept the change. They answer for what the team does as a result.

Learning outcomes and assessment criteria

LO1
The learner will: Know how people in a department respond when their roles change.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
1.1Analyse the effects on the work of a department when the roles within it change
1.2Evaluate what is at stake for different groups of people in a department when its roles change, and the reasoning behind the positions they take
1.3Compare different approaches to working with people through a change to their roles, and the reasoning behind each
1.4Evaluate the reasons changes to roles are agreed and then not carried through in practice
1.5Identify the obligations and constraints that govern how own department may work with people whose roles change, including consultation requirements, agreements and the organisation's own procedures

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner analyses how the team's work changes as roles shift (1.1). They evaluate what is at stake for field sales, inside sales and content producers, including targets and commission (1.2). They compare approaches to working with people through the change (1.3). They evaluate why agreed changes slip back, such as representatives returning to private spreadsheets (1.4). Commission terms and consultation procedures are identified at 1.5.

LO2
The learner will: Be able to establish how a change to roles affects the people in a department.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
2.1Identify the people whose roles change and state what changes for each, and identify the people whose work depends on the roles that change
2.2Determine the method used to establish what those people raise about the change, and state the reasons for choosing it
2.3Establish, using that method, what each person or group raises about the change, and record it
2.4Analyse what was raised to establish which points concern the change itself and which concern the way it is being made
2.5Interpret what was raised to establish which parts of the change are least likely to be carried through in practice, and state the reasons
2.6Evaluate the reliability of what the method established, and state how the position of people who did not take part was handled

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner identifies whose roles change and who depends on them, such as a finance colleague who relies on CRM forecasts (2.1). They determine how to hear what people raise, perhaps team meetings plus one-to-ones (2.2), and record it (2.3). They separate objections to automated lead routing from objections to how territories were moved (2.4). They judge what is least likely to stick (2.5) and who was missed (2.6).

LO3
The learner will: Be able to determine how a department will respond to people who do not accept a change.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
3.1Determine the criteria against which the department's response to each point raised will be evaluated, and state the reasons for them
3.2Analyse the points raised by people who do not accept the change, and evaluate which of them are supported by evidence
3.3Determine which points will change the department's plans and which will not, and state the reasons in each case
3.4Use relevant investigation of comparable changes, inside or outside own organisation, to inform the response
3.5Adapt the department's plans in line with the points determined at 3.3, and state what changed
3.6Determine what the department will do where a person continues not to accept the change, within the obligations and constraints identified at 1.5

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner sets the criteria for judging the team's response to each point (3.1). They test objections against evidence (3.2). One example is a claim that AI-drafted emails get fewer replies, checked in the team's outreach records. They determine which points change the plan (3.3), use comparable changes (3.4) and adapt (3.5). They decide what happens if someone still disagrees, within the limits at 1.5 (3.6).

LO4
The learner will: Be able to work with the people whose roles change.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
4.1State to each person whose role changes what is changing, when it changes, and what is expected of them
4.2Respond to each point raised, stating what the department will do about it and the reasons
4.3Conduct a discussion with a person who does not accept the change, and record what was agreed and what was not
4.4Determine the support each person requires to carry out the changed role, and state how and when it will be provided
4.5Determine how the department will keep the people whose roles change informed while the change proceeds, and how the effect on their work will be measured

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner tells each person what changes, when, and what is expected (4.1). An example is a rule that a person checks every AI-drafted proposal before it reaches a client. They answer each point raised (4.2). They hold a recorded discussion with someone who has said they do not accept the change (4.3). They determine each person's support (4.4), how people stay informed and how the effect is measured (4.5).

LO5
The learner will: Be able to evaluate how a department worked with the people whose roles changed.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
5.1Evaluate the effect of the change on the work of the people whose roles changed, against what was determined at 4.5
5.2Evaluate the effect of the change on the department's work, using figures from the department's own systems
5.3Evaluate how far the points recorded at 2.3 changed what the department did, giving reasons
5.4Evaluate how effective the method determined at 2.2 and the criteria determined at 3.1 were, giving reasons
5.5Identify what would be determined differently at the next change to the department's roles, and the reasons

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner evaluates the effect on the changed roles against 4.5 (5.1). They evaluate the effect on the team's work from its own pipeline or campaign figures (5.2). They judge how far the points recorded at 2.3 changed what the team did (5.3). They review their method and criteria (5.4) and what they would decide differently next time (5.5).

5 learning outcomes, 27 assessment criteria. The same criteria as the generic Diploma, word for word.

Evidence from Sales and marketing work

  • 2.1. A map of the roles that change, such as business development representatives and a campaign executive. It shows the colleagues outside the team who depend on their work.
  • 2.2, 2.3, 2.6. A consultation plan with its reasons and a record of what each role raised. Colleagues appear by role or as Colleague A, with a note on who did not take part.
  • 2.4, 3.2, 3.3. An analysis separating objections to automated lead routing from objections to how it was introduced. Each is tested against the team's outreach records, with a decision on the plan.
  • 4.3. A record of a discussion with Colleague A, who stated they do not accept the change. It shows what was agreed and what was not, backed by witness testimony.
  • 4.4, 4.5. A support and communication plan for the changed roles, including any reasonable adjustments. It states how the effect on their work will be measured.
  • 5.1, 5.2. A review against the measures set at 4.5, using the team's own CRM activity and pipeline report. It states the period the evidence covers.

Keeping it at Level 5

It drops to Level 4 when a supplied change script or rollout template decides 2.2, 3.1 and 3.3. It rises above Level 5 when the learner redesigns commission across the business, which belongs at 1.5 as a constraint.

The unit aim, level check, boundaries, assessment guidance and evidence trail are in ZFF-EI-05 on the generic Diploma, and apply here unchanged.

ZFF-AU-05

Planning Automation Across a Department

Level5TQT80 hoursCredits8GLH46 indicativeStatusMandatoryCriteria26

In Sales and marketing

Sales and marketing teams repeat many processes. They qualify leads, log calls, build proposals and quotes, schedule posts and send email campaigns. They prepare account review packs and the weekly report. The learner works out which could be automated, which should not be, and what it would cost to find out. The unit stops at a recommendation to whoever decides.

Learning outcomes and assessment criteria

LO1
The learner will: Know how automation changes the work of a department.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
1.1Analyse the effects that introducing automation has on the work of the people in a department
1.2Compare different approaches to introducing automation into a department, and the reasoning behind each
1.3Evaluate the reasons automation programmes fail to deliver what was expected of them
1.4Identify the constraints that limit what own department can automate, including systems, contracts, permissions and skills
1.5Evaluate the different views held within own department about automation, and the reasoning given for them

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner analyses how automation changes people's work, such as representatives no longer researching each prospect by hand (1.1). They compare approaches, such as one campaign stream first against the whole lead process at once (1.2). They evaluate why sales automation disappoints, such as lead scores nobody trusts (1.3). CRM permissions, data rules and agency contracts are constraints at 1.4, and team views are weighed at 1.5.

LO2
The learner will: Be able to establish what a department does and where its effort goes.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
2.1Map the processes carried out by own department, showing inputs, outputs and the people involved
2.2Determine the method used to establish where the department's effort goes, and state the reasons for choosing it
2.3Establish the volume and the time cost of the department's main processes from the department's own systems
2.4Identify the processes that other teams depend on, and what they depend on them for
2.5Evaluate the reliability of the figures obtained, and state how gaps were handled

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner maps processes from enquiry to signed proposal, or from campaign brief to published post (2.1). They determine how to find where effort goes, such as CRM activity logs plus a short time sample (2.2). They establish volume and time cost from those systems (2.3). They identify what other teams depend on, such as handover notes (2.4), and how reliable the figures are (2.5).

LO3
The learner will: Be able to evaluate processes in a department as candidates for automation.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
3.1Determine the criteria against which candidate processes will be evaluated, and state the reasons for them
3.2Analyse a candidate process to establish which parts could be automated and which could not
3.3Interpret the costs and the benefits of automating a candidate process, using figures from the department's own systems
3.4Use relevant investigation of comparable work, inside or outside own organisation, to inform the evaluation
3.5Identify a process that should not be automated, and evaluate the reasons
3.6Evaluate the candidate processes against the criteria determined at 3.1, and state which are recommended

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner sets the criteria a candidate must meet (3.1). They analyse a process such as proposal writing to see which parts could be automated (3.2). Costs and benefits come from the team's own figures (3.3), tested against comparable teams (3.4). They name a process to keep manual, such as pricing exceptions for key accounts (3.5). Then they recommend against their own criteria (3.6).

LO4
The learner will: Be able to work with the people whose work automation would change.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
4.1Identify the people whose work would change, and how it would change for each
4.2Consult those people about the proposed change, and record what was raised
4.3Analyse the concerns raised, and evaluate which of them alter the evaluation
4.4Adapt the evaluation in response to what the consultation established, and state what changed
4.5Evaluate the skills the department would need that it does not currently hold

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner identifies whose work would change and how (4.1), then consults them (4.2). A representative might warn that automated follow-ups would reach people who asked not to be emailed. The learner decides whether concerns like this alter the evaluation (4.3) and adapts it (4.4). They evaluate the skills these automations need that the team lacks (4.5).

LO5
The learner will: Be able to recommend a course of action and evaluate own method.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
5.1State the checks, the fallbacks and the points of human decision for each recommended process
5.2Evaluate the risks the recommendation carries for the department, and what would be done about each
5.3Present the recommendation, with the evidence, to the person who would decide
5.4Evaluate how effective the method determined at 2.2 and the criteria determined at 3.1 were, giving reasons
5.5Identify what would be determined differently in a further evaluation, and the reasons

Applied in Sales and marketing

For each recommended process the learner states the checks, fallbacks and points of human decision (5.1). One example is a person approving every generated claim before a campaign goes out. They evaluate the risks to the team, such as breaking the electronic marketing rules (5.2). They present to the person who would decide (5.3). They review their method (5.4) and what they would change next time (5.5).

5 learning outcomes, 26 assessment criteria. The same criteria as the generic Diploma, word for word.

Evidence from Sales and marketing work

  • 2.1, 2.4. A process map of the team's lead handling, proposal and campaign work. It shows inputs, outputs, people and the teams that depend on each process.
  • 2.2, 2.3, 2.5. A note on how effort was measured, with volumes and time costs from the team's CRM and email platform. It states how gaps were handled.
  • 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.6. The learner's own criteria and an evaluation of candidates such as call logging and proposal drafting. Costs come from the team's figures, ending in a recommendation.
  • 3.5. A reasoned case for keeping one process manual, such as replies to complaints raised on social media.
  • 4.2, 4.3, 4.4. A consultation record with colleagues identified by role. The revised evaluation shows what changed.
  • 5.1, 5.2, 5.3. The recommendation as presented, with checks, fallbacks and points of human decision. It carries a risk table covering PECR and UK GDPR, and witness testimony of the presentation.

Keeping it at Level 5

It drops to Level 4 when the processes are already chosen and a supplied business case template decides 3.1. It rises above Level 5 when the recommendation changes how the whole organisation sells, instead of recording that need at 1.4.

ZFF-DA-05

Using Data to Direct a Department's Priorities

Level5TQT70 hoursCredits7GLH40 indicativeStatusMandatoryCriteria25

In Sales and marketing

Sales and marketing teams hold many measures. Pipeline value, conversion by stage, cost per lead, open rates, renewals and attributed revenue are common. Each encourages some behaviour and leaves something out. The learner uses the team's own data to decide where its effort should go, and may change what it measures. What the organisation needs the function to achieve is set elsewhere.

Learning outcomes and assessment criteria

LO1
The learner will: Know what a department's measures show and what they drive.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
1.1Analyse what the measures reported by own department actually count, and over what period
1.2Analyse the behaviour each measure encourages in the people whose work it reports on
1.3Evaluate what own department's current measures leave out
1.4Compare different approaches to measuring work of this kind, and the reasoning behind each
1.5Evaluate the different views held within own department about what its measures show, and the reasoning given for them

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner analyses what each measure counts and over what period (1.1). For example, does a qualified lead mean the same in marketing and sales reports? They analyse the behaviour each measure drives, such as call targets that reward volume (1.2), and what it leaves out (1.3). They compare measuring approaches, such as different ways of attributing a sale, with their reasoning (1.4). They weigh the team's views (1.5).

LO2
The learner will: Be able to determine a question about a department's priorities that data could help settle.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
2.1Determine the question about own department's priorities that the work will address, and state the reasons for selecting it
2.2Determine the data that bears on the question, and state the reasons for the selection
2.3Identify data that was available but set aside, and evaluate the effect of setting it aside
2.4Determine the method to be used to work with the data, and state the reasons for choosing it
2.5Evaluate the quality of the data obtained, and state how gaps and errors were handled

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner determines a question about the team's priorities (2.1). One might be whether account managers should spend more time on renewals than new business. They determine the data that bears on it (2.2) and identify what they set aside (2.3). They determine the method (2.4) and evaluate the data's quality, such as duplicate contacts or stages updated late (2.5).

LO3
The learner will: Be able to analyse a department's data and interpret what it indicates.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
3.1Analyse the selected data in relation to the question
3.2Interpret what the analysis indicates about where the department's effort is going
3.3Identify an interpretation the same data would also support, and evaluate which of the two it better supports
3.4Use relevant investigation, inside or outside own organisation, to test whether the interpretation holds
3.5Evaluate the limits of what the data can show, and what would be needed to settle the question
3.6Identify where an AI or automated tool was used in the analysis, and evaluate what was checked and why

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner analyses the data against the question (3.1) and interprets where effort is going (3.2). They find a second reading the same data supports and weigh the two (3.3). Renewals might look strong only because difficult accounts moved to another team. They test the reading through comparable work (3.4) and state the data's limits (3.5). They say where an AI tool was used and what they checked (3.6).

LO4
The learner will: Be able to direct a department's priorities from what data indicates.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
4.1Determine the changes to the department's priorities that follow from the interpretation
4.2Evaluate what the department would stop or reduce in order to make the changes possible
4.3Consult the people whose work the changes would affect, and record what was raised
4.4Adapt the proposed changes in response to what the consultation established, and state what changed
4.5Present the proposed priorities, with the evidence, to the person who decides them, and respond to challenge
4.6State how the effect of the changes will be measured, and over what period

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner determines the change to priorities (4.1). They evaluate what the team would stop to make room, such as a low-yield event (4.2). They consult the people affected (4.3) and adapt the proposal (4.4). They present it to the person who decides the team's priorities and answer challenge (4.5). They state how the effect will be measured, and over what period (4.6).

LO5
The learner will: Be able to evaluate the effect of directing priorities from data.
3 criteria
RefThe learner can
5.1Evaluate the effect of the changed priorities against what was stated at 4.6, using evidence
5.2Evaluate how effective the method determined at 2.4 was, giving reasons
5.3Identify what the department would measure differently, and what would be determined differently next time, and the reasons

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner evaluates the effect against 4.6, using at least one measurement taken after the change (5.1). They evaluate the method determined at 2.4 (5.2). They identify what the team would measure and decide differently next time (5.3). An example is retiring a measure that rewarded the wrong behaviour.

5 learning outcomes, 25 assessment criteria. The same criteria as the generic Diploma, word for word.

Evidence from Sales and marketing work

  • 1.1, 1.2, 1.3. An annotated copy of the team's own pipeline report. It shows what each measure counts, the behaviour it drives and what it misses.
  • 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4. A question note stating the priority question, the data chosen and set aside, and the method. Each choice has its reasons.
  • 2.5, 3.1, 3.2. The analysis, done in the learner's own tools, with a data quality note on duplicate contacts and stale opportunities.
  • 3.3, 3.5, 3.6. Two readings of the same campaign or pipeline data, compared, with the limits of what it shows. It declares any AI tool used and what was checked.
  • 4.3, 4.4, 4.5. A consultation record by role and the adapted proposal. Witness testimony covers the presentation and the challenge answered.
  • 4.6, 5.1. The measure and period stated in advance, and a review after at least one later measurement. It states what the evidence cannot yet show.

Keeping it at Level 5

It drops to Level 4 when a supplied question, reporting pack or fixed attribution model removes 2.1 and 2.4. It rises above Level 5 when the learner reconsiders the organisation's revenue targets rather than what the team counts.

The unit aim, level check, boundaries, assessment guidance and evidence trail are in ZFF-DA-05 on the generic Diploma, and apply here unchanged.

ZFF-PJ-05

Applied Project: Annual Automation Plan for Own Department

Level5TQT140 hoursCredits14GLH10 indicativeStatusMandatoryCriteria30

In Sales and marketing

The brief is an annual automation plan for the learner's own sales, marketing or account management team. Nothing else is stated. The learner maps the team's year, including renewal cycles, trade events and seasonal campaigns. They cost the options from the team's own figures and consult the people affected. Then they present the plan to whoever signs off the team's plans.

Learning outcomes and assessment criteria

LO1
The learner will: Be able to establish what own department does and what it costs.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
1.1Determine the boundary of the department the plan will cover, and state the reasons for it
1.2Map the processes the department carries out across a year, including those that occur only occasionally
1.3Establish the volume, the time and the cost of each main process from the department's own systems
1.4Determine the method used to establish those figures, and state the reasons for choosing it
1.5Evaluate the reliability of the figures, and state how gaps and disputed figures were handled
1.6Identify the obligations and commitments the department must continue to meet whatever the plan changes

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner determines the boundary, such as whether marketing operations sit inside the plan (1.1). They map the year's processes, including rare ones such as annual price updates and event follow-up (1.2). They establish volume, time and cost from the team's systems (1.3) and determine the method (1.4). They evaluate the figures, including disputed ones (1.5), and identify what must still be met, such as consent records (1.6).

LO2
The learner will: Be able to analyse which of a department's processes are candidates for automation.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
2.1Determine the criteria by which candidate processes will be selected, and state the reasons for them
2.2Analyse each main process against those criteria
2.3Interpret the cost and the benefit of automating each candidate, using the department's own figures
2.4Use relevant investigation of comparable work to inform the evaluation, and state what it established
2.5Identify the processes that should not be automated, and evaluate the reasons for each
2.6Evaluate the candidates against one another and state the order in which they are recommended

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner sets the selection criteria (2.1) and analyses each main process against them (2.2). Costs and benefits come from the team's own figures (2.3). They investigate comparable work and state what it established (2.4). They identify processes to keep manual, such as negotiating terms with key accounts (2.5). Then they put the candidates in order (2.6).

LO3
The learner will: Be able to consult the people whose work a plan would change.
5 criteria
RefThe learner can
3.1Identify the people whose work each recommended change would affect, and how it would affect them
3.2Consult those people, and record what was raised
3.3Analyse the concerns raised and the reasoning given for them, and evaluate which of them change the plan
3.4Adapt the plan in response, and state what changed and the reasons
3.5Evaluate the skills the department will need that it does not currently hold, and state how they will be obtained

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner identifies who each change affects, such as campaign executives if email builds are automated (3.1). They consult those people (3.2) and analyse the concerns and reasoning given (3.3). They adapt the plan (3.4). They evaluate the skills this plan needs that the team lacks, and how they will be obtained (3.5).

LO4
The learner will: Be able to produce a sequenced annual plan with checks and fallbacks.
7 criteria
RefThe learner can
4.1Sequence the recommended changes across the year, and state the reasons for the order
4.2Identify the dependencies between the changes, and between the changes and work outside the department
4.3State the resources each change requires, and when they are required
4.4State the checks that will be carried out on each change, by whom, and at what point
4.5State the fallback for each change, and the point at which the fallback would be used
4.6Evaluate the risks the plan carries for the department, and state what would be done about each
4.7Determine how the effect of each change will be measured, and against what starting figure

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner sequences changes around the team's year, such as not moving lead routing just before a major event (4.1). Dependencies include the CRM administrator or the website team (4.2). Resources, checks, fallbacks and risks are stated for each change (4.3 to 4.6). Each change has a measure and a starting figure (4.7).

LO5
The learner will: Be able to present a departmental plan and evaluate own method.
6 criteria
RefThe learner can
5.1Present the plan to the person who signs off the department's plans, in a form suited to that decision
5.2Respond to challenge on the plan's figures, its sequence and its risks
5.3Record the decision taken and any conditions attached to it
5.4Evaluate how effective the method determined at 1.4 and the criteria determined at 2.1 were, giving reasons
5.5Evaluate how far the consultation changed the plan, giving reasons
5.6Identify what would be determined differently in the next annual plan, and the reasons

Applied in Sales and marketing

The learner presents the plan to the person who signs off the team's plans (5.1). They answer challenge on its figures, sequence and risks (5.2). The decision and any conditions are recorded (5.3). They evaluate their method and criteria (5.4) and how far consultation changed the plan (5.5). They identify what they would decide differently next year (5.6).

5 learning outcomes, 30 assessment criteria. The same criteria as the generic Diploma, word for word.

Evidence from Sales and marketing work

  • 1.1, 1.2, 1.6. A year map of the team's processes with the boundary stated. It lists the obligations that continue, such as consent records and contract terms.
  • 1.3, 1.4, 1.5. A cost table built from the team's CRM, email platform and time records. It states the method and how disputed figures were settled.
  • 2.1, 2.3, 2.5, 2.6. The learner's own selection criteria and a costed evaluation of each candidate. It names the processes kept manual, with reasons, and the recommended order.
  • 3.2, 3.3, 3.4. A consultation record kept across the year, with colleagues identified by role. A change log shows how the plan moved in response.
  • 4.1, 4.2, 4.4, 4.5, 4.7. The plan itself, sequenced across the year, with dependencies and checks. It names who carries out each check, when each fallback is used, and each starting figure.
  • 5.1, 5.2, 5.3. The presentation pack, witness testimony of the challenge, and the recorded decision with any conditions.

Keeping it at Level 5

It drops to Level 4 when a process list, a supplied funnel model or a business case template decides 1.2, 2.1 or 2.3. It is above the level when the plan reshapes how the organisation goes to market. That need belongs at 4.2 as a dependency.

The unit aim, level check, boundaries, assessment guidance and evidence trail are in ZFF-PJ-05 on the generic Diploma, and apply here unchanged.

Section 5

Assessment

This version is assessed exactly as the generic Diploma: by portfolio from real work, decided by a human assessor, with a recorded professional discussion for every unit. See assessment and quality assurance and the evidence trail on the generic Diploma.

Section 6

What we know is not yet right

Listed plainly, so that a reviewer has this list before finding any of it.

1

No sales or marketing practitioner, and no assessor with sales or marketing experience, has read this version.

2

The rules listed are for teams working in the UK. A team that markets to people abroad works under other laws too, and this version does not cover them.

3

Several examples assume the team keeps a CRM and an email platform with activity records. A team without them needs another source of figures for ZFF-AU-05 2.3 and ZFF-PJ-05 1.3, and this version does not say which.

4

Everything open on the generic Diploma applies here too. See its open items.
